draft.title: Interpolation and extrapolation
card: A least-squares line can be used to predict values. The range of the data runs from the smallest to the largest x-value in the data set.
Interpolation
predicting for an x-value inside the range of the data. It is fairly reliable, because the line is built from data on both sides of that value.
Extrapolation
predicting for an x-value outside the range of the data. It is less reliable, because the pattern may not continue beyond the data.
Example: a line is fitted to data for x from 10 to 40. Predicting at x = 25 is interpolation. Predicting at x = 60 is extrapolation.
draft.remember: Inside the data range is interpolation and fairly reliable. Outside it is extrapolation and less reliable.

a.q: A least-squares line is fitted to data with x-values from 20 to 50. Which prediction is extrapolation?
opts: Predicting y when x = 70
Predicting y when x = 35
Predicting y when x = 22
Predicting y when x = 48
a.why: The value x = 70 is outside the range of 20 to 50, so it is extrapolation. The values 22, 35 and 48 all lie inside the range, so they are interpolation, even 22 and 48, which sit close to the ends.
a.clue: Compare each x-value with the data the line was built from.

b.q: Dana has hours of study (from 2 to 10 hours) and test scores for 30 students. Her least-squares line predicts scores at 6 hours and at 14 hours. Which statement is correct?
opts: The 6 hour prediction is more reliable than the 14 hour one
The 14 hour prediction is more reliable than the 6 hour one
Both predictions are equally reliable, as they use one line
Neither prediction is reliable, as it is only an estimate
b.why: The value 6 hours is inside the range of 2 to 10, so it is interpolation and fairly reliable. The value 14 hours is outside the range, so it is extrapolation and less reliable, even though both use the same line.
b.clue: Which prediction has data on both sides of it?

b.best: The 6 hour prediction is more reliable than the 14 hour one
